chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Harun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said to me: 'They concealed the Basmala (In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful). By Allah, they have concealed the best of names.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he entered his house and the Quraysh were gathered against him, would say loudly 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful' and raise his voice with it, so the Quraysh would turn and flee.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed regarding that: 'And when you mention your Lord alone in the Quran, they turn their backs in aversion.'

key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: The Basmala, the opening phrase of Quranic chapters meaning 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful'
key_terms.قُرَيْشٌ: The Quraysh, the dominant tribe of Mecca during the Prophet's time
key_terms.نُفُوراً: Aversion or turning away with disgust

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) recite the Basmala loudly to make the Quraysh flee?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the Quraysh concealed the 'Basmala' due to their aversion to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) reciting it loudly upon entering his home, a practice that caused them to flee in disgust. This specific incident is linked to the revelation of Quran 17:46, illustrating how the Quraysh turned away when the Lord was mentioned alone, highlighting the tension between public proclamation and private concealment of divine names in early Meccan society.
